title: Introduce progressive retrieval resilience quickstart
author: Asha Patel
description: Summary: Adds a new quickstart that demonstrates progressive retrieval and resilient tool-calling patterns for RAG-powered agents. Motivation: many production retrieval flows face intermittent vector DB latency and partial index availability; progressive retrieval (fetch early, return partial results, continue background fetches) combined with graceful fallback policies reduces tail latency and improves user-perceived responsiveness. This quickstart exposes concrete patterns (incremental fetch, circuit-breaker for remote search, local prefix cache warmup, staged scoring) and wiring for telemetry and stepwise assertions that teams can plug into Redwood Quickstarts. Design: - Introduces a small Node TypeScript example runner (src/runner.ts) that: 1) starts by querying a lightweight local index for quick hits; 2) returns initial answer candidates immediately while continuing to fetch deeper results from an external vector DB (simulated with delay); 3) merges results with confidence-aware scoring; 4) demonstrates tool-calling fallback (call external API only if confidence < threshold). - Includes a sample serverless config for deploying to Redwood-hosted quick environments and a Docker recipe for an isolated devloop. - Adds telemetry probes: latency histograms for first-byte, completion, vector-db tail; counters for fallback trigger, partial-response served, and resumed-completion success. - Adds a small set of step assertions and an example smoke test harness (smoke/partial-response.test.ts) that validates partial responses within a 350ms median under simulated DB latency. How to use: - Clone and run locally: npm ci && npm run dev:quickstart - The runner exposes /query which returns an initial partial response and includes a status header X-RAG-STATE: partial|final - Configuration knobs are in quickstarts/progressive-retrieval/config.yaml: thresholds, warmup size, circuit-breaker windows, telemetry sample rate. Checklist before merge: - [x] Example code implemented and tested locally - [x] Telemetry keys added to Console dashboard templates - [x] Developer docs written with step-by-step runbook - [x] Smoke CI added to repo quickstart suite - [x] Reviewed and approved by two runtime/telemetry engineers Notes on scope: This quickstart intentionally simulates intermittent external DB latency (to keep the example small) rather than integrating a cloud provider vector DB. The patterns shown are portable to real DBs (we include wiring comments and a small adapter). Related: ENG-5123 (progressive retrieval prototype), PM-211 (customer ask: perceptible search tail).

release_notes: Add progressive retrieval quickstart demonstrating partial responses, resilient fallback policies, and telemetry probes; includes smoke CI and console dashboard template.
notes_for_changelog: This quickstart is a developer reference for progressive retrieval patterns to reduce tail latency in RAG flows. It provides a minimal runner, adapter, telemetry wiring, and smoke tests.
testing_instructions: Run npm ci && npm run dev:quickstart. Use curl -v 'http://localhost:8080/query?q=example' to see initial partial response and later final response. Run smoke tests: npm run test:smoke
risk_assessment: Low: example code is isolated in quickstarts/progressive-retrieval. It only references internal telemetry schemas and adds a new CI job. No changes to runtime library code.
